title: Podcast Video Editor | Long-Form Interview + Social Clips
description:
We’re looking for a thoughtful video editor to shape an already-filmed interview into an engaging full episode and compelling social clips.

The conversation covers entrepreneurship, creativity, identity, and life transitions. We need someone with strong storytelling instincts: someone who can spot a great moment, build a strong opening, and keep a conversation flowing naturally.

Deliverables
- One 60–80-minute horizontal interview.
- One 30-second teaser.
- 6 vertical highlight clips.
- One 2–3-minute behind-the-scenes video.
- English and Chinese subtitles for the main episode and highlight clips.
What we’re looking for
- Experience editing podcasts, interviews, or documentary-style content.
- Good judgment around pacing, emotional moments, humor, and hooks.
- Confidence with multicamera footage, audio cleanup, color matching, and vertical reframing.
- Clean subtitles and tasteful graphics.
- Clear communication and reliable turnaround.
The style should feel polished and personal, with space for meaningful moments to breathe. We’d love an editor who brings ideas about the story and which moments deserve their own clips.

Strong English comprehension is essential. Mandarin is a plus. The conversation is primarily English with some Chinese-language exchanges; please explain your approach to bilingual subtitles.

Working together
We’ll provide footage, creative direction, and branding guidelines, with consolidated, timecoded feedback. Final handover should include exports, subtitle files, and organized editable project files.

This is a fixed-price project with potential for ongoing work. We’re targeting an early-December release.

Project identities and unpublished footage are confidential. Further details will be shared with shortlisted candidates under a confidentiality agreement.

To apply, please send:
1. Two or three relevant samples, including a long-form interview and a short clip. Specify your role.
2. Your language skills and subtitle workflow.
3. Your availability, first-cut timeline, and quote for the full package, including revision allowance and whether translation is included.
4. A timestamp from one sample where you made a strong editorial choice, with a sentence explaining why.

ONLY CANDIDATES WHO SUBMIT ALL FOUR ANSWERS TO THE QUESTIONS WILL BE CONSIDERED.

Shortlisted applicants may be invited to a small paid editing test, with scope and fee agreed in advance.

title: Short-Form Video Editor for Founder-Led DTC Brand (Instagram Reels)
description:
I'm the founder of a growing golf brand in the U.S., and I'm looking for a talented short-form video editor to help turn my raw founder footage into engaging, story-driven Instagram Reels.

Most videos will be around 45–60 seconds and will typically start with footage of me speaking directly to camera. I'll provide the raw footage, script, and access to brand assets/B-roll when needed.

However, I'm NOT looking for someone who simply cuts out pauses, adds captions, throws in my B-roll, and calls it done.

I'm looking for an editor with strong creative judgment who understands storytelling, pacing, hooks, retention, music, and how to keep a short-form video visually interesting.

I want you to bring your own creativity to the edit.

If you think a section needs additional B-roll, a screenshot, graphic, sound effect, music, animation, screen recording, or another visual element, I want you to recognize that and add it. You should also be comfortable sourcing appropriate external B-roll or visual assets when it makes the story better rather than relying entirely on what I provide.

I can also provide examples of videos and editing styles I like so you have a strong reference for the direction I'm going for.

The goal is simple: I want to eventually be able to send you my raw footage + script and trust you to turn it into an engaging finished video without me having to tell you where every cut, B-roll clip, or visual should go.

### About the content

Our product is a golf glove, so a lot of our content is built around founder-led storytelling rather than simply showing the product.

Topics might include how I started the company, mistakes I've made building the brand, how our products are made, what makes them different, customer stories, our mission and giveback, industry recognition, and the behind-the-scenes reality of building a golf brand.

The editing should help tell that story.

I'm looking for videos that feel orgranic, natural, fast-moving, and engaging without being obnoxiously over-edited. Think strong visual storytelling—not random effects just for the sake of keeping something on screen.

### Project details

- Typical finished video: 45–60 seconds
- Format: Vertical 9:16
- Rate: $100 per finished video
- Project-based/freelance work
- Potential for consistent future projects if we're a great fit
- I'll provide raw footage, scripts, brand assets, and creative references
- You should be comfortable sourcing additional appropriate visuals/B-roll w

description:
I’m a gaming content creator looking for an experienced long-form YouTube editor who understands **Madden, College Football, and the sport of football itself.** I want someone who can turn a competitive game into a story that keeps viewers watching from the opening hook to the final play.

You’ll take approximately **30–40 minutes of raw footage** and build an engaging YouTube video. The finished length should serve the story—keep the moments that matter and cut what slows it down.

**What I’m Looking For**

- **Strong storytelling:** Identify the game’s storyline and build around it—rivalries, trash talk, momentum shifts, costly mistakes, comebacks, and clutch plays.
- **YouTube pacing:** Create a strong opening hook, cut dead time, and keep viewers invested throughout the video.
- **Football knowledge:** Understand why a play, adjustment, down-and-distance situation, or coaching decision matters.
- **Authenticity:** Preserve the competitive tension, natural reactions, humor, and back-and-forth with my opponent. Viewers should be able to follow the game and feel its stakes.
- **Purposeful editing:** Use zooms, captions, replays, music, and sound effects to enhance key moments without overwhelming the gameplay or dialogue.
- **Independent judgment:** Review the footage, find the best moments, and shape the story without needing timestamps or instructions for every cut.

**The Style**

My content is built around competitive football gaming, personality, trash talk, and real reactions. I want viewers to feel like they’re watching a great matchup with a creator they enjoy spending time with.

The edit should give big moments room to breathe while keeping the overall video moving. Knowing when to let a conversation or play unfold is just as important as knowing when to cut.

**Requirements**

- Proven experience editing long-form YouTube gaming content.
- Strong understanding of storytelling, pacing, and viewer retention.
- Familiarity with Madden and/or College Football.
- A solid understanding of football rules, strategy, and game situations.
- Reliable communication, consistent delivery, and openness to feedback.

**To Apply, Please Include**

1. Two or three relevant long-form videos you personally edited, preferably sports gaming.
2. A brief explanation of how you would approach turning a full game into a compelling story.
3. Your experience with Madden, College Football, and football in general.

- Dynamic on-screen captions throughout for low-volume / sound-off viewing
- Phrase-based captions with important words highlighted, rather than lazy one-word-at-a-time subtitles

- Punch-ins, zooms and reframing where appropriate
- Highlighting parts of equations or whiteboards as they’re being explained
- On-screen questions, multiple-choice answers and timers
- Simple low level motion graphics and animated text
- Sound effects used intentionally rather than on every cut
- Visual changes throughout the video to help maintain attention
- Humour/reaction editing when the format calls for it

The goal is not overly flashy editing. The Maths still needs to be easy to understand. We want someone who understands how to make educational content entertaining without making it distracting.

Important
Up to this point, I have been editing all of the videos myself, so there is already an established standard and style for the content. I’m now looking for someone who can take over that workload while maintaining that standard. The chosen editor should be able to produce work that is at least on par with the current edits, ideally better.

This means I’m not simply looking for someone who can cut footage together and add captions. I’m looking for someone who can understand why an edit works, make strong creative decisions, and improve the pacing, clarity and retention of the content.

we may instead want the viewer to see something like:

You will work directly with a creative strategist. You will get a brief for every video: the angle, the script, the voice, the music, and visual direction. But the brief is direction, not a spec sheet. The design of the video is yours.

1 to 2 videos per week. Not five. We are not optimising for volume. We would rather have two videos that were genuinely designed than five that were assembled.

Examples of what we expect
https://www.instagram.com/p/DaAiSmyNav7/

https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=1493190448827610
https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=2284000695462199

This is the level. Watch all four before you apply. Look at the pacing, the sound design, the captions, the way the visuals sit against the voice.

We are not looking for these to be recreated. We are looking for someone who can work at this level and bring something we haven't done yet.

If this is not the kind of work you want to be doing, this is not the role.

What you'll actually do:

Plan before you cut. Every video starts with a creative direction — how it will open, where it turns, how it will feel. You decide that, not the timeline.

Choose the visuals. We have a library with thousands of clips. The brief points you at a direction. Which specific shot goes on which specific line is your call, and it should be defensible.

Design the sound. Not just placing a music track. Sound effects, texture, risers, impacts, ambience. Where the sound carries the video, and where it gets out of the way.

Analyse the music properly. We give you the track. You work out where the beat should build, where to hold tension, where to release it, where the momentum turns, and how the script's biggest line lands on top of it. This is one of the biggest differences between a good ad and a great one.

Design the voice. Generating a file in ElevenLabs is not voice work. We want someone who processes it — EQ, compression, de-essing, saturation, space — so it sounds recorded, not generated. And who re-times the pauses by hand instead of accepting what the model gave them.

Captions. Clean, considered, designed. Typography that suits the video. Not a default auto-caption preset dropped on top.

title: Video Editor for Hip-Hop Documentary YouTube Channels (25–40 min videos, long-term)
description:
I run multiple YouTube channels in the rap niche, and I need good editors with experience to join the team. The videos are hip-hop documentaries: the stories behind rappers, their money, their beefs, their families, and what actually happened behind the headlines.

This isn’t a one-off gig. If you’re good, there’s steady, ongoing work.

What the work looks like

Videos run 25 to 40 minutes.
You get a finished script and a voiceover. Clips are marked in the script with the source, a link and exact in/out timestamps.
You turn that into a documentary people actually want to watch to the end.
That means finding and cutting footage to match every line: interviews, news clips, music videos, live performances, paparazzi footage, social media posts, court documents, headlines, photos.
It also means pacing the story, adding sound design and music, and adding text and graphics where they help the story land.

What I need from you

Proven rap or hip-hop documentary experience. Send me videos you’ve edited for channels in this niche. General YouTube editing isn’t enough. You need to know the culture, the artists and the footage that exists for them.
You know who you’re looking at. If the script says Gucci Mane in 2009, I don’t want a clip from 2020. If it says Lil Wayne’s daughter, I don’t want a random girl. The wrong footage kills the video.
Every clip matches what was just said. If the narration sets up a clip, the clip has to pay it off. If a clip doesn’t fit what’s being said, it shouldn’t be there.
You follow instructions. I give detailed scripts and specific notes. I need someone who reads them properly and sticks to them, not someone who does their own thing and makes me fix it after.
Retention-focused editing. No dead air, no lazy stock footage on loop, no 20 seconds of the same image. Keep it moving, especially in the first 2 minutes.
Strong footage sourcing. You know where to find rare interviews, old news segments and deep-cut clips, not just the first YouTube result.
Sound design and music that fit the mood: tension, money, lifestyle, emotional moments.
Clean motion graphics: headlines, document callouts, money figures, timelines, maps and name tags. Simple and sharp, not over the top.
Copyright awareness. You know how to use clips in a way that keeps the channel safe from claims and strikes.
Fast, reliable turnaround. Tell me realistically how long a 30-minute video takes you.

description:
I run Basic Wisdom, a financial education channel providing securities licensing exam preparation (SIE, Series 63, 65, 66, Series 7). I am releasing a brand-new 9-unit NASAA Laws & Regulations video course on YouTube—publishing 3+ long-form videos per week (usually 5–15 minutes each).

Key Responsibilities:

Clip Selection & Hooking: Review raw 5–15 minute course videos, identify the highest-value 30–90 second teaching moment, key exam trap, or practice question walkthrough, and craft a strong opening hook.

Vertical Editing: Reframe widescreen 1080p footage into 9:16 vertical format using proper safe zones (ensuring no UI/caption overlap on Reels/Shorts).

On-Screen Polish: Add clean, accurate captions/subtitles, subtle text callouts for key financial terms, and strategic visual zooms/cuts to maintain retention (polished educational style, NOT chaotic meme editing).

Consistency: Produce 3 to 5 vertical clips per week with fast turnarounds tied directly to my weekly YouTube upload schedule.

Ideal Candidate:

Proven experience editing short-form educational, talking-head, or financial/business content. Fluent in English with high accuracy in financial/technical terminology captions. Proficient in Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or CapCut Pro. Strong understanding of platform retention metrics, hook optimization, and native layout safe zones.

Bonus: Ability or desire to take on full long-form video editing (5–15 min lessons) as this role scales!

Our audience is mostly women into fitness and clean eating, but we want to still focus on overall fitness market. What we need
A creative who can take our raw footage and brand assets and turn them into finished content and ads that perform on TikTok and Meta. Three kinds of work:

1. Organic short-form clips — the bulk of the work. Street-style interviews, taste tests, "guess the macros," founder talking-to-camera, behind-the-scenes. Classic TikTok editing: strong hook in the first 2 seconds, tight cuts, trending sounds, SFX, zooms, native captions. Natural and unpolished-on-purpose, but clearly finished and built to be watched to the end.
2. Paid video ads — short direct-response cuts (15–30s) from the same footage: hook, product/macros, CTA. with and without burned-in captions, plus hook variations for testing.
3. Static and motion ad graphics — Meta/TikTok/Pinterest image ads, carousels, and simple animated graphics (macro callouts, "before/after," ingredient comparisons, testimonial cards) using our brand fonts and colors. You should know what a high-performing CPG static ad looks like and be able to design one in Canva, Figma, or Photoshop.

If it goes well, we'll move to a regular cadence

You're a fit if you
- Have made both video and static ad creative for food, beverage, CPG, or wellness brands — link 3+ examples of each and note which performed
- Understand direct-response fundamentals: hooks, pattern interrupts, social proof, clear CTA, ad-safe text density for Meta
- Know current TikTok/Reels trends, sounds, and pacing without being told
- Can write or suggest hooks and ad copy, not just execute what you're handed
- Use CapCut and/or Premiere for video, and Canva/Figma/Photoshop for graphics; comfortable following brand guidelines
- Are responsive and can turn work around in 2–4 days once we're ongoing

Ben

title: Train an AI Agent to Edit Our Short-Form Ads in Our House Style. $500 Fixed, Paid on Results
description:
We're a marketing agency. We put out about 100 short-form videos a month: vertical 9:16 Meta and Instagram ads and reels, shot on cinema cameras.

We already use an AI agent that edits with ffmpeg, plus HTML/CSS animations rendered in headless Chromium (Playwright). It's close, but not at the level we need. We want someone to train and set it up so it edits our videos the way we like, consistently, without us fixing them afterward.

THE STYLE: FOUR HORSEMEN
The look we want is the Four Horsemen style (Four Horsemen Media / @fourhorsemen short-form edits). If you don't know their work, study it before applying. In short, that means:
- Cinematic, premium and clean. Nothing cartoonish, no cheap templates or stock-looking effects
- Fast pacing with constant movement: punch-ins, zooms and cuts on almost every beat so the viewer never gets bored
- Bold, clean captions that pop word by word, with the key word highlighted
- Heavy sound design that you can feel: whooshes on every cut, pops on text, risers, hits and subtle bass impacts
- Motion graphics, b-roll and overlays that reinforce what's being said, timed exactly to the voice
- Strong hook in the first 1 to 2 seconds
If your samples don't show you can hit this level, this job isn't a fit.

What matters most to us:
- Transitions that feel smooth and intentional (whips, push-ins, light leaks, film burns)
- Captions with strong typography, a highlight on the keyword, and timing synced tightly to the voice
- Sound design: whooshes, soft pops on graphics, risers and subtle impacts, mixed so you can actually hear them
- Animations that pop in at the right moment and never cover the speaker's face
- Music that's clearly audible but sits under the voice, and never sounds cheesy

What you'll deliver:
1. A reusable style system the agent can follow: caption styles, transition presets, an SFX map, graphic templates, and rules for timing and placement.
2. Written instructions or skills the agent loads, so any new raw clip goes through the same process.
3. A QC checklist the agent runs before delivery.
4. 3 finished test ads that the agent makes on its own from raw footage we provide, using your setup, at Four Horsemen quality.

How payment works:
- $500 fixed, paid in full only when we are 100% satisfied with the result. Total satisfaction is required.
- The job is done when the agent produces the 3 test ads on its own, at our standard, with zero manual fixes from us.

I am a physician and owner of ESPRIMED, an aesthetic medicine practice in Switzerland. I will provide video footage, additional product or treatment information, my logo and branding guidelines.

Your tasks:
• Edit the footage into a polished Reel with an attention-grabbing opening and a clear structure.
• Incorporate relevant information from my materials through text overlays, graphics or suitable supplementary visuals.
• Create accurate German subtitles.
• Optimise audio and colours, add appropriately licensed music if needed, and incorporate my logo.

Requirements:
Native or excellent German is essential, as the footage and final content will be in German. You should have experience editing Reels, ideally in aesthetic medicine or skincare. I am looking for someone who works independently and contributes thoughtful content suggestions. All medical statements and the final version require my approval.

An MP4 in vertical 9:16 format, versions with and without subtitles, the editable project file and two revision rounds.

Please send relevant work samples, details of your German proficiency, your fixed price for ONE test Reel and your estimated turnaround time.

title: Youtube and Reels
description:
We need someone who can take existing podcast recordings and short educational videos and turn them into polished, engaging social media content for Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and LinkedIn. We want someone who can identify compelling moments, create attention-grabbing openings, and help communicate meaningful messages that encourage viewers to watch, engage, share, and take action.

Primary Responsibilities
1. Podcast Editing & Content Repurposing: 

Review full-length podcast episodes and identify the most engaging, educational, emotional, or thought-provoking moments.

Create approximately 3–5 short-form video clips per podcast episode, depending on available content.

Edit clips into 30–60-second reels.

Identify compelling opening statements that capture attention within the first 3 seconds.

Add professional captions, transitions, background music when appropriate, and branded elements.

Recommend moments that could become standalone social media posts.

Create short promotional videos announcing new podcast episodes.

2. Weekly Social Media Video Editing

Edit approximately 2–3 short educational videos per week, typically 30–60 seconds.

Remove unnecessary pauses, mistakes, and distractions while preserving Dr. Shannon's natural speaking style and personality.

Add readable captions, engaging opening text, and clear calls to action.

Incorporate tasteful humor, emphasis, or creative editing when appropriate.

Format videos for Instagram Reels, Facebook Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and LinkedIn.

3. Branding & Creative Direction

Maintain consistent colors, fonts, logos, and visual styling across content.

Create engaging video covers or thumbnails with strong, searchable titles.

Use a polished, professional visual style that appeals to leaders, executives, professional women, and individuals interested in mental wellness.

Keep content warm, relatable, culturally aware, and trauma-informed.

Recommend creative improvements that increase engagement without sensationalizing mental health topics.

4. Content Strategy & Organization

Help identify recurring themes from podcast episodes that can become future content.

Suggest hooks, video titles, and short captions when needed.

Organize completed videos in shared folders.

Maintain a simple content calendar and deliver approved content on schedule.

Provide final videos ready for uploading to social media.

title: Instagram Reels Video Editor for Hair Transplant Clinic — Long-Term Remote
description:
We're a growing hair transplant clinic in Los Angeles, CA, seeking a reliable Instagram Reels editor for long-term remote work. We have a large library of raw footage: procedures, before-and-after results, educational clips, and talking-head videos. We need someone to turn it into polished Reels that build trust and attract patients.

Our style is modern and premium, in line with leading international hair-transplant surgeons. We'll share reference accounts for inspiration, not copying.

What you'll do

	•	Pick the strongest moments from raw footage
	•	Edit 15–60 second Reels with a strong hook in the first 2 seconds
	•	Add animated captions, music, sound effects, and transitions
	•	Do basic color correction and audio cleanup
	•	Apply our branding and calls to action
	•	Suggest hooks and concepts to improve engagement
	•	Deliver in 9:16 at 1080×1920

Ideal candidate

	•	Has a strong short-form portfolio (Reels, TikTok, or Shorts)
	•	Understands hooks, pacing, and retention
	•	Is comfortable with close-up surgical footage
	•	Communicates reliably and meets deadlines
	•	Uses Premiere Pro, After Effects, CapCut, or similar
	•	Medical, aesthetic, or personal-brand experience is a must

Paid test: $100
The test is one 20–45 second Reel with a hook, captions, music, and color correction. It includes one revision and is due within 2–3 days. If it's a good fit, we'll move to ongoing work.

Ongoing: 3–5 Reels per week, paid per Reel or as a monthly package.

Confidentiality: All patient footage is confidential. It may not be shared or added to your portfolio without written permission.

title: Video Editor for Swimwear Reels
description:
We’re a small swimwear brand looking for a reliable editor to turn raw try-on footage into short vertical videos for TikTok, Instagram Reels and ads.

What you’ll be doing:

Cutting through raw clips and picking the best moments
Syncing cuts to a trending sound or beat
Adding a short text hook at the start
Occasionally writing a short POV-style script for a voiceover
Simple captions and on-screen text
One our best performing videos is this: https://www.instagram.com/p/DcN3pCIhPC_/ so we would want more in a similar style, as well as others that are different, but from this video you can see this is not complex editing. No motion graphics or After Effects needed. It’s simple, repetitive work that rewards care and consistency and an understanding of what our customers like.

Who we’re looking for
We’re not looking for a high-end video editor. We’re looking for someone who:

Lives on TikTok and Reels. You scroll every day, you notice trends, and you have a natural feel for what makes someone stop and watch.
Is quick and comfortable in CapCut (or a similar editing app). You can cut, sync to a beat and add text without overthinking it.
Has a good eye for the best moment. You can look through a few minutes of footage and pick the 3 seconds that matter.
Enjoys repetitive work. You find a rhythm in editing similar videos and take pride in doing each one well.
Is creative with words. You can come up with a scroll-stopping hook or a short, relatable POV line. Good written English is important here.
Is reliable. You meet deadlines, reply to messages, and let us know early if something comes up.
Takes feedback well. You’re happy to adjust, learn what works for us, and get better over time.
Wants something long-term. We’d love to find one person we can keep working with and grow alongside.

Experience with fashion, swimwear or lifestyle content is a bonus, but not required. If you’re early in your editing journey but have a great feel for short-form content, we’d still love to hear from you.

Paid test task
Shortlisted applicants will receive a paid test: one batch of raw footage to edit into a finished 15 to 30 second video.

title: Creative Video Editor & Content Producer for Instagram Reels + TikTok
description:
## Creative Video Editor & Content Producer | Instagram Reels + TikTok

I'm building a personal content brand around a simple philosophy:

**An interesting life isn't something you have. It's something you build.**

I have hundreds of photos and videos documenting travel, fashion, design, beauty, adventures, relationships, and everyday life. I also have a distinctive voice, a strong point of view, and more creative ideas than I have time to execute.

I'm looking for a talented short-form video editor who is also a **creative storyteller and idea generator**.

I don't just need someone to assemble clips. I want someone who can look at a collection of seemingly unrelated photos, find an interesting story, and turn it into something people stop scrolling for, watch, and want to share.

### The creative vision

My content should make people think:

**"She makes me want to do more with my own life. And I feel like we'd be friends."**

The style is smart, witty, provocative, visually sophisticated, occasionally irreverent, and authentically aspirational without feeling unattainable.

Think strong editorial storytelling, surprising humor, beautiful visuals, and genuine personality.

This is NOT an account about aging, luxury for luxury's sake, generic motivation, or traditional influencer content.

### What you'll do

- Review curated collections of my existing photos and videos.
- Pitch creative concepts, scroll-stopping hooks, and compelling storylines.
- Create polished, engaging 15–45-second Instagram Reels and TikToks.
- Add music, text overlays, transitions, and thoughtful visual pacing.
- Identify unexpected connections between different experiences.
- Suggest new content ideas and recurring creative formats.
- Eventually help mine my larger photo archive for stories worth telling.

### The $100 paid creative trial

I'll provide approximately 20–30 personal photos spanning different experiences.

You'll deliver:

1. Two proposed opening hooks and a brief creative concept.
2. One finished 20–30-second vertical Reel.
3. Music, text overlays, and polished editing.
4. One round of revisions.
5. A platform-ready 1080 × 1920 video export.

**The challenge:** Make viewers feel inspired to do something interesting with their own lives, rather than simply admire someone else's.

title: eCommerce Growth Manager | TikTok Shop, Creator Affiliates & Sales
description:
eCommerce Growth & Marketing Lead – TikTok Shop, Creator Affiliates & Sales

Arctic Chaga is an established, family-owned Alaskan company specializing in wild-harvested Alaskan chaga, functional mushroom coffees, and our signature Mushroom Power 5K blend.

We've spent years developing our products, building our brand, and establishing retail relationships. We believe we have the product quality, sourcing, and story to eventually compete with major brands like RYZE, MUD\WTR, and Everyday Dose. But we understand that building a successful national brand takes more than having great products.

We're looking for someone with the marketing experience and leadership skills to help us get there.

Our family handles harvesting, processing, manufacturing, and shipping. We don't have the marketing expertise to do everything ourselves. We need someone who can take charge of our marketing, make decisions, develop a plan, and personally execute it without us having to manage every detail.

We already have an established WooCommerce website, product bundles, subscriptions, an approved US TikTok Shop, AffiliateWP Pro, RewardsWP Pro, Stripe Connect, existing email marketing and abandoned-cart systems, product videos, and marketing materials.

We also have a valuable marketing opportunity from blind product comparisons we've conducted against established mushroom brands. We believe those experiences, along with our Alaskan sourcing story and product demonstrations, could become strong selling tools if presented effectively and with properly supported claims.

What we need is someone who knows how to turn these assets into customers and sales.

We have a particular approach in mind for the first 30 days, although we're open to improvements from someone with proven experience.

First, we want to build our affiliate and creator network. We'd like to identify and begin recruiting 15–25 qualified micro-creators in wellness, coffee, functional foods, and related markets. We need someone who can personally handle outreach, follow-up, onboarding, and coordination of product promotions. We're looking for creators who can generate actual purchases, not just followers or views.

Second, we want to activate our TikTok Shop. It's already approved but barely being used. We need someone to optimize the listings, establish creator affiliate partnerships, coordinate shoppable videos, and start building a functioning sales channel.

description:

WHAT YOU'LL DO
 
- Get started on TikTok with the name, bio and profile picture we provide.

- Spend a few minutes in the app each day, scrolling the feed and interacting naturally with content in our theme, so you stay close to our audience.
- Be open to small changes we ask for along the way, as things grow.
 
PAY

- $10 bonus when one of your posts passes 1M views within 48 hours of posting (one bonus per 2-week payment).
- As we grow, good assistants get more accounts, and more pay with them.
 
REQUIREMENTS
 
- You live in the US and use a US mobile carrier.
- A smartphone and a few free minutes every day.
 
WHAT WE VALUE MOST
 
Consistency and attention to detail. Once you have the Drive folder, the posts go out every day on time without us having to remind you, and every post goes out exactly as we prepared it. Quick replies in the first few days while you learn, and after that it runs on its own.
 
That's it. If you're interested, write the word "pink" at the start of your proposal and tell me a bit about how you use TikTok.

Nous recherchons des créatrices francophones pour des missions régulières : skincare, maquillage, soins du corps et des cheveux.

La mission (1 concept)
- 1 script fourni par nous, avec 3 hooks différents (les premières phrases de la vidéo)
- 2 hooks de réserve en plus, fournis dans le script, à tourner pendant la même session
- Tournage face caméra du produit, que nous vous envoyons
- Vidéo finale de 15 à 30 secondes environ

Ce que vous livrez
- Les rushes bruts, avec chaque hook dans un fichier séparé
- Format vertical 9:16, Full HD (1080 x 1920) minimum, 4K bienvenue
- Lumière naturelle ou douce, son clair sans bruit de fond, pas de musique ni de filtre
- Le montage, les sous-titres et le CTA sont réalisés par nos soins

Délai
Tournage et livraison sous 3 jours ouvrés après réception du produit.

Révisions
Jusqu'à 2 révisions incluses par concept, si une prise ne respecte pas le script ou les consignes techniques (prise floue, texte oublié, son inaudible).

Droits d'usage
- Usage publicitaire payant (Meta, TikTok) pendant 3 mois, inclus dans le prix
- Usage organique sur les comptes de la marque, sans limite de durée
- Merci d'indiquer votre tarif pour prolonger les droits pub à 6 et 12 mois

Budget
De 90 à 150 € par concept, tout compris: 3 hooks, 2 hooks de réserve, 2 révisions et 3 mois de droits pub. Nous privilégions les créatrices disponibles pour plusieurs missions par mois.

Profil recherché
- Français courant, à l'aise face caméra, ton naturel et spontané
- Intérêt réel pour la beauté et le soin
- Smartphone récent et un espace calme et lumineux pour tourner
- Portfolio UGC ou vidéos face caméra existantes. Les débutantes motivées sont bienvenues si vous pouvez montrer une vidéo test.

Pour postuler, répondez à ces questions :
1. Partagez 2 ou 3 vidéos face caméra (UGC, TikTok, Reels).
2. Quel est votre tarif pour 1 concept, avec 3 hooks, 2 hooks de réserve, 2 révisions et 3 mois de droits pub inclus ?
3. Quel est votre tarif pour prolonger les droits pub à 6 et 12 mois ?
4. Combien de missions pouvez-vous prendre par mois ?
5. Quels types de produits beauté utilisez-vous au quotidien ?



ENGLISH
Savyn is a UGC agency specializing in beauty brands that sell online. We write the scripts and handle the editing. You bring your natural on-camera presence.

What we need
• A UGC video of about 20 to 35 seconds, vertical 9:16.

We are not looking for AI avatars, stock footage or UGC actors. We will provide a library of our own video and picture content, professionally shot and phone shot, by many different people on many different days. Your job is to make it look like one brand and cut it into ads that stop the scroll and get people to book.

Two campaign tracks:

1. General salon ads (color, cuts, blondes, the team, the new salon). Five concepts. Goal: book an appointment.
2. Hair extension ads. Three concepts. Goal: book an extension consultation or appointment. These use only real extension photos and videos.

Each concept is delivered as a 9:16 master (1080x1920) and a 4:5 recomposition (1080x1350), burned-in text inside Meta's safe zones, no voiceover, no music (the agency adds licensed music in Ads Manager), plus the primary text and headline you would run with it. Videos 10 to 25 seconds with two hook variants. We expect roughly five videos, two statics and one carousel across the eight.

How it runs: milestone 1 is one extension video and one general static from a starter kit we send you, due within three days of kickoff ($400). If it is right, milestone 2 is the other six concepts, due ten days later ($1,400). We pay milestone 1 either way. This is a one-time project; if it goes well we may come back, but nothing beyond the $1,800 is promised.

You must be hands-on in Premiere or DaVinci, After Effects (or equivalent for clean text animation), and Photoshop (color matching, retouching, compositing). Beauty, fashion or salon work in your portfolio is a strong plus. Native-level English for on-screen copy.

To apply, answer the screening questions and link two paid-social ads you cut from a client's own footage (not stock, not AI). Tell us what you changed in the edit and why.

description:
You’ll spot the ads and posts that are already winning, and turn them into our next ones before anyone else does.

We run a small group of brands across business education, membership communities, AI software and digital products. We follow a set of brands and creators whose ads and content perform. We need someone to watch that market closely, pull out what’s working and turn it into ready to use ideas for our brands every week.

This is not an entry level role, and it’s not a role where you’ll be taught how to do it. We need someone who has done this before, can start within days and takes work off our plate from week one.

What you’ll do

Use our research tools to track ads and organic content across the brands and creators we follow.
Find the outliers: the ads that have run longest, the posts that beat a creator’s average, the hooks and formats getting real traction.
Break down why each one works: the hook, the angle, the format, the offer and the audience it speaks to.
Turn those findings into repurposing ideas for each of our brands, with hooks, angles and format notes ready for our creators and designers.
Spot gaps in our marketing strategy and tell us what we’re missing, without being asked.
Deliver a weekly research and ideas report on a set day, every week, without chasing.

Who you are

You have a proven track record in ad research, creative strategy or content strategy, with results you can show.
You know Meta Ad Library and social content research inside out, and you pick up new tools quickly.
You understand direct response marketing: hooks, angles, offers and buying psychology.
You work to a schedule and hit your deadlines without reminders.
You use your own initiative. When something isn’t clear, you make a sensible call and flag it rather than waiting.
You bring ideas. We want a fresh perspective, not someone who only does what’s on the list.

Who this isn’t for
If you need detailed instructions, regular check-ins to stay on track or training in how to do the role, this won’t be the right fit. We need help now, not after a training period.

How to apply
Start your proposal with the word “OUTLIER” so we know you’ve read this in full. Then include:

Two or three examples of ad or content research you’ve done, and what came of it.
One ad or post you’ve seen recently that you’d repurpose, and how you’d adapt it for a business membership or an AI software brand.
Your availability and how soon you can start.

title: Native Spanish speakers from Bogotá, Colombia for a short vowel recording project
description:
BoldVoice is an AI-powered English accent coaching app. We're building speech models that recognize vowel sounds, and we need native Spanish speakers from Bogotá to record a short set of held vowels. This is a small, fixed-price project ($10 per speaker) that takes about 30 minutes, with the opportunity for more work.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR
5 native Spanish speakers who grew up in Bogotá (or the surrounding Cundinamarca area) and speak with a Bogotá accent. Both men and women are welcome.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
We'll send you a simple web recording page. It walks you through each vowel, records in your browser, and gives you one file to send back to us.

You'll record the 5 Spanish vowels as steady, held sounds:
- i (as in "sí")
- e (as in "té")
- a (as in "la")
- o (as in "no")
- u (as in "tú")

For each vowel you'll record 2 takes. In each take you'll hold the vowel 5 times, with a short silence between holds. The page shows you when to hold and when to rest:
- Hold the vowel steadily for 5 seconds, keeping the same sound from start to end without sliding into another vowel.
- Rest for 2 seconds in silence.
- Repeat until you've done all 5 holds (about 40 seconds per take).

You'll also record 5 seconds of silence at the start so we can hear the room.

RECORDING SETUP
- A quiet room, with no music, TV, fans or other voices in the background
- A computer with Chrome and a working microphone
- Speak at a normal, comfortable volume

DELIVERABLES
- The recordings file from the recording page
- Delivery within 3 days of starting the contract

REQUIREMENTS
- Native Spanish speaker from Bogotá
- A quiet space and a computer with a microphone
- Able to follow simple recording instructions

HOW TO APPLY
Please answer the two screening questions. No resume needed.

- First batch: the Spanish letter-sound set plus a small set of words and minimal pairs — short clips to judge, recording replacements wherever the machine take falls short of a native ear.
- Ongoing batches as we stage more Spanish content (word recordings, sentence clips) — we're looking for people available for repeat work.

description:
We are looking for a talented motion designer to develop the visual identity of Il Palcoscenico dell’Anima (The Stage of the Soul), an Italian video podcast featuring musicians, actors, writers and other creative professionals.

Through intimate conversations, we explore the psychological and emotional dimensions of artistic expression, creativity, identity and personal experiences.

Creative direction and color palette

Our visual identity is based on three main colors:

* Pink: from delicate blush and dusty pink to more vibrant shades.
* Purple: from soft lavender and lilac to deep violet.
* Light blue: from pale, airy blue to more intense and luminous shades.

We would like these colors to blend harmoniously through gradients, subtle lighting effects, atmospheric transitions and sophisticated visual compositions.

The overall aesthetic should be artistic, cinematic, elegant, emotional and contemporary, with a sense of depth, imagination and introspection.

We want something visually memorable, avoiding generic corporate graphics, overly playful designs or conventional psychology-related imagery.

Required deliverables

* Creative visual concept and art direction
* Animated podcast intro (8–12 seconds)
* Coordinated animated outro
* Animated guest names and titles
* Editable YouTube thumbnail template
* Reusable Instagram Reels graphics
* Editable source files

We particularly appreciate experience in cinematic title sequences, cultural productions, documentary storytelling, music projects and artistic branding.

Please share your portfolio, hourly rate and estimated hours for completing the project.

Our guiding philosophy:

“Here, art is not merely something we create. It is something that reveals who we are.”

title: Podcast Music Composer Needed
description:
NAC is seeking a freelance composer to develop an original musical identity for our upcoming external podcast. We’re looking for music that reflects NAC’s personality: curious, warm, collaborative, grounded, confident, and a little unexpected. The music should make you curious about what you're about to hear, not tell you how excited you're supposed to feel.

The right sound should feel professional without feeling corporate, polished without feeling generic, and playful without becoming quirky. A little funk or groove is welcome. We’re open to acoustic, electronic, or blended approaches and especially interested in distinctive instrumentation, texture, rhythm, and musical ideas that evolve rather than simply loop.

Creative direction:
• Curious, human, warm, and confident
• Distinctive and slightly unexpected
• Room for groove, personality, and experimentation
• Sophisticated enough to support thoughtful conversations without becoming overly serious
• Flexible enough to work beneath speech and across different episode topics

Please avoid: hand claps, finger snaps, whistling, ukulele, stomps, cymbal swells, pulsing kick drums, predictable inspirational builds, or other conventions associated with generic corporate music.

If it could soundtrack almost any company's corporate video, it probably isn't right for this use.

Anticipated deliverables include:
• 10–20 second intro
• 20–30 second outro
• Several 2–5 second transitions/bumpers
• Loopable music bed

We’re looking for a composer who can create a sonic identity, not simply background music, and who is excited to interpret an established visual and verbal brand through sound.

Note: We request that AI-generation is not utilized in the composition of these tracks.

About us
We’re Dave Inglis and Dr. Jen Forristal: coaches, facilitators, parents, and the authors of Chief Family Officer and The Umbrella Effect. Our work is called Live Undefended. We help leaders, couples and families notice the armor they’ve learned to wear (the performing, the people-pleasing, the need to be right) and build the capacity to show up honestly at work and at home. Much of our work is with families, because that’s where the stakes are highest and where the most important conversations happen.

Our new weekly podcast, Undefended, brings that work to life through real, unscripted conversations with each other and our guests. Before this we hosted Poco a Poco. Now we’re looking for a creative partner to turn these conversations into content that reaches the people who need it.

The role
This is an ongoing contract role of 1–2 days per week, with real potential to grow into something more permanent. We’ll give you the raw footage from each weekly episode plus other materials. You’ll turn them into finished content and own the execution and distribution from there.

Who you are

A strong video editor with an instinct for the moment worth sharing: the line that lands, the honest pause, the story that hooks
Fluent in how YouTube and Instagram work, including formats, hooks, captions and analytics
Skilled at thumbnail and visual design
Organized, self-directed and happy to own a process end to end
Drawn to honest, human content. Bonus if personal growth, relationships, parenting or leadership interest you.
Experience with Descript is a strong plus (it’s our main tool)

Details

Contract, 1–2 days per week, ongoing, with potential to grow
Fully remote, anywhere in the world
$15–$50 USD per hour, depending on experience. Fit matters more to us than rate: we’re looking for someone great who connects with what we do.

Send us links to your portfolio, ideally including short-form clips and thumbnails you’ve made, plus a few lines on why this work speaks to you.

Bi-weekly publishing

| **Show Notes** | Short summary, bulleted key takeaways, and standard boilerplate/disclaimer text. |

What started as an independent production has grown quickly in its first year, becoming a top 10 US business podcast and "Instant Hit Show" on Spotify, gaining 100,000 YouTube subscribers, and reaching millions of viewers monthly, featuring interviews with top founders and CEOs, including the leaders of Airbnb, Microsoft, Rivian, NYSE, Samsung, Canva, Poppi, Peloton, Revolve and Away.

Here's a link to our channel: https://www.youtube.com/@BehindtheBusinessShow

We aim to bring the editorial rigor and journalistic standards of traditional media to a new generation of digital-first storytelling, while giving audiences a closer look at the people behind top consumer brands.

With ambitious plans for what's next, this is an opportunity to work closely with the host and a lean, creative team, contribute to the show's editorial and creative direction, and help shape the next chapter of a new media brand from the ground up.

What you'll do

Editorial development:

- Turn extensive research and background documents into compelling, well-structured and fact-checked interview scripts that reflect the host's voice, editorial sensibility and high standards for accuracy.
- Pitch and script short-form explainer videos and other editorial content around global business, markets, technology, consumer trends and relevant news.
- Help develop episode trailers, social videos and other editorial elements, with the support of an associate producer and video editors by picking soundbites and suggesting fun production or visual design ideas.

Creative production & post-production oversight:

- Plan and manage the weekly post-production schedule, coordinating with editors and keeping deliverables on track.
- Review and approve episode cuts, trailers, social clips, thumbnails and other video assets, providing clear, constructive editorial and creative direction to editors and ensuring all deliverables meet the show's editorial, visual and branding standards.
- Select compelling episode thumbnails for testing, pitch strong headlines and angles that are engaging without being sensationalist, and create accurate, consistent show notes for each episode.

title: YouTube Podcast Video Editor – Long-Term, 4–6 Episodes/Month (Premiere Pro)
description:
I'm looking for a reliable, detail-oriented video editor to help produce a YouTube podcast focused on faith and culture.

The podcast features thoughtful conversations and occasional long-form commentary. I'm looking for someone who can consistently deliver clean, professional edits while helping maintain a high standard of quality across each episode.

This is an ongoing opportunity for the right person, with approximately 4–6 episodes to edit each month.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Edit 45–60 minute podcast episodes for YouTube. Clean up and refine footage to create a polished, engaging viewing experience.

Add simple graphics, titles, and other basic visual elements as needed. Make straightforward cuts and edits without overcomplicating the production.

Work in Adobe Premiere Pro. Occasionally help troubleshoot recording issues or provide remote guidance via screen sharing for our EVMUX setup.

The editing style is clean, professional, and straightforward. I'm not looking for elaborate animations, flashy transitions, or complicated graphics.

WHAT I'M LOOKING FOR

Experience editing YouTube podcasts or long-form video content. Proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro.

Strong attention to detail and consistency. Good English comprehension, especially when editing conversations about faith, culture, and related topics.

Reliable communication and the ability to meet deadlines. Someone interested in building a long-term working relationship.

Familiarity with EVMUX or similar recording setups is a plus, but not a requirement.

WORKLOAD & ARRANGEMENT

Approximately 4–6 episodes per month. Episodes are typically 45–60 minutes long.

Less than 30 hours per month, depending on episode or commentary length. Fully remote.

Ongoing work, with the potential for a long-term relationship. I'm looking for someone dependable who can become a consistent part of the podcast production process.

HOW TO APPLY

Please include the following in your proposal:

* A brief introduction and your experience editing podcasts or YouTube videos.

* A link to 1–2 examples of your editing work, preferably long-form content.

* Your experience with Adobe Premiere Pro.

* Your typical turnaround time for a 45–60 minute podcast episode.

I'm especially interested in finding someone who is reliable, communicates well, and takes pride in producing quality work.

I look forward to hearing from you. Thanks very much!

title: Podcast Editor | Short Form Editor | Virtual Assistant
description:
High Ticket AI Systems is an acquisition-first B2B podcast agency. We book the guests and produce every show, and our editing team turns each recording into a finished episode and a set of short clips. You would edit and publish episodes for our own show and our clients' shows.

How the editing works

You will edit with Claude, using an editing process we have already built and documented. Claude reads the transcript, picks the strongest moments, and renders the cuts. Your job is to run it, check every cut by eye and ear, and make sure nothing goes out with a mistake.

You do not need to be a Premiere or DaVinci expert. You do need a sharp eye for a strong clip and an ear for a bad cut.

What you will do

Podcast episodes
- Download the raw recordings from Riverside (each person's video and audio track)
- Run the edit with Claude: the open hook, the full episode and the audio cleanup
- Check every cut by ear before anything ships
- Write the episode title, description and show notes, and make the thumbnail
- Publish every episode through Riverside to YouTube, Spotify and Apple Podcasts

Short form
- 3 vertical shorts per episode, with captions and B-roll
- A short hook title on each one
- Check captions for misspelled names and misheard words

Virtual assistant
- Keep files organized in Google Drive
- Stay responsive in Slack during your working hours
- Handle admin tasks as they come up

Requirements
- Fast, reliable internet. You will move large video files every day. A speed test screenshot is required with your proposal.
- A backup connection, like a mobile hotspot, for when your main internet drops
- A computer (Windows or Mac) with at least 16 GB of RAM that can render 4K video
- Daily Slack user
- Experience with Riverside and publishing to YouTube, Spotify and Apple Podcasts
- Comfortable using Claude, or able to learn it fast. You will work in Claude Code, which runs in a terminal. No coding needed, but you should not be afraid of it.
- Strong written English
- You know what makes someone stop scrolling on a short
- At least 4 hours a day overlapping with US Mountain Time

To apply

1. Start your proposal with the word "Riverside" so we know you read this
2. Attach a speed test screenshot from speedtest.net
3. Link 2 or 3 short form clips you edited
4. Tell us in 1 sentence how you have used Claude or another AI tool in your work
5. Share your weekly availability in hours and your time zone

Long term role for the right person.

title: Video editor to cut long-form podcast footage into short-form reels (health-tech brand)
description:
We are a US telehealth platform for clinician-led, personalised health protocols. We are recording a 1.5-hour podcast with our two co-founders, covering the business, peptides, the patient journey, founder stories, and access to personalised healthcare. We need an editor to turn that raw footage into short-form videos for Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn and X.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Review the full recording and pull out the strongest 30–90 second moments

• Edit each clip into a vertical (9:16) reel with tight pacing, clean cuts and no dead air

• Add accurate, styled captions on every video, since most people watch without sound

• Write a short hook on screen in the first two seconds of each clip

• Match our brand look (we'll send fonts, colours and examples)

• Deliver files ready to post, plus 1:1 and 16:9 versions where we ask for them

HOW WE WORK
• We build reels around a set of keywords that repeat across 6–8 videos, so you'll get a keyword list with each batch and should pick clips with that in mind

• Because we're in healthcare, captions and on-screen text must match exactly what was said. Please don't shorten or reword anything that changes the meaning of a health statement. We review every clip before it goes live.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
• A portfolio that includes podcast-to-reel work (please link at least three examples)

• Experience with Premiere Pro, Final Cut, DaVinci Resolve or CapCut

• Good judgement on which moments will hold attention, not just technical editing

• Reliable turnaround and clear communication across time zones (we work across Australian Eastern and US Eastern time)

• Health, wellness or interview-format experience is a plus

SCOPE AND BUDGET
• First batch: 10-15 reels from one 1.5-hour recording
• Ongoing work is available if the first batch goes well

TO APPLY
Tell us which of your past clips you're most proud of and why you chose that moment. We'd then like to set up a short call to talk through the project.

title: Podcast Producer for Women's Health App
description:
About us
We're a women's health app on iOS and Android that helps women understand how hormones shape their health at every life stage. We're a small, founder-led startup in San Francisco, and you'd work directly with our CEO.

About the role
You'll build our podcast from zero to a consistent weekly or biweekly show. You'll own production end to end, from shaping the format and booking guests to editing, publishing and turning each episode into clips for social.
Guests will include clinicians, researchers and women sharing their own health stories. The tone is evidence-forward and warm: plain-spoken science, real conversations, no fear-mongering and no wellness clichés. You'll work directly with the CEO, who will often host.

What you'll do
Show development
• Shape the show's format, segments, episode length and release cadence with the CEO
• Build and maintain an editorial calendar of topics and guests
• Research each topic and write episode outlines, interview questions and show notes

Guests and booking
• Source and book guests: physicians, researchers, practitioners and community voices
• Handle guest prep, scheduling, recording logistics and release forms

Production
• Run remote recordings (e.g. Riverside) and occasional in-person sessions
• Edit audio and video for clarity and pacing; mix, level and master
• Manage music licensing (we use Epidemic Sound) and intro/outro assets
• Publish episodes through Spotify for Creators and distribute to Apple Podcasts, YouTube and other platforms

Repurposing and growth
• Cut each episode into short vertical clips with on-screen captions for Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts
• Write titles, descriptions and SEO-friendly show notes, plus transcripts
• Coordinate guest cross-promotion and track downloads, retention and follower growth
• Report monthly on what's working and recommend changes

Quality and accuracy
• Fact-check health claims and flag anything that needs clinical review before release
• Keep the brand voice consistent: accurate, empowering and community-minded

What you bring

Must have
• 2+ years producing a podcast or audio/video series, with episodes you can share
• Strong editing skills in  Riverside's editor
• Comfort turning long-form video into short, captioned social clips
• Solid working knowledge of podcast hosting, RSS and distribution
• Organized and self-directed; you can run a production calendar without being chased
• Clear writing for show notes, outlines and guest outreach

title: Video Podcast Editor for Cinematic Interview Series (Premiere, Riverside XML)

WHAT YOU GET FROM ME

title: Short-Form Video Editor (Reels/TikTok/Shorts): Ongoing Work for Creators, Podcasts & Brands
description:
We're ReelForge, a UK short-form video editing agency. We turn our clients' raw footage into scroll-stopping Reels, TikToks and YouTube Shorts. Our clients include podcasters, coaches and experts, YouTubers and TikTok creators, and small brands and businesses.
We're building a small team of **reliable editors for ongoing work** (starting at around 10–25 clips a month and growing)
We send you the client's raw footage: a podcast or talking-head video (often 20–60 minutes), phone clips, vlogs or product/brand footage.
 You **choose the best moments** and cut them into **vertical clips (9:16), 30–60 seconds** each.
 **Animated, word-by-word captions** with key words highlighted.
A **hook title** on screen in the first 2 seconds.
 Remove pauses and filler words. Keep it punchy.
 Quiet **royalty-free** background music (commercial use OK).

*What we care about most:** being **on time**, clear communication, and following the brief. Great editing matters, but reliability matters even more
How we hire:** we'll pick a few applicants for **one paid test clip** (same footage and brief for everyone). The best 2–3 get regular monthly work.

To apply, please answer the questions below.** Applications without answers won't be considered.

1.. Please share links to **3 short-form clips** you edited (vertical, with captions). Ideally a mix, for example a podcast or talking-head clip, a creator video and a brand or product video.
2. What is your price for **1 clip** (up to 60 s, from our footage, with animated captions and a hook)?
3. What is your price **per clip** if we send you **one 60-minute episode and ask for 10 clips** from it?
4. How much extra for **b-roll + sound effects**, and for **extra formats** (1:1 and 16:9)?
5. What's your usual **delivery time**, and can you reliably deliver within **24 hours**?
6. How many clips can you handle **per week**?
7. Do you only use **royalty-free music and stock footage** that our clients can post commercially?
8. What time zone are you in, and when are you usually online?

description:

Verify views and report campaign results.

Help us scale successful campaigns.

Clipping

Post 1 clip a day for each assigned client on Instagram, Facebook and YouTube Shorts

Set up and warm up new clip accounts for new clients

Research creators and businesses and keep our lead list organized
Book and confirm calls, and send reminders
Pull numbers for client reports every 15 days

Keep the shared inbox organized and flag anything important

Later

Train new clippers and check their work in their first 2 weeks

You use Instagram, Facebook and YouTube every day and know what makes a good short clip
Organized and reliable. You don’t miss deadlines, and you speak up early when something is wrong
Clear written English
Comfortable with Google Sheets, Google Drive and WhatsApp
Able to post between 8am and 6pm Pacific Time (US)
Reliable internet and a computer
Bonus: you’ve clipped, edited or run social media pages before (CapCut or similar)

Hours and pay

Up to 6 to 8 hours a day, Monday to Friday
When work is light, some days are shorter or off, with the same pay
Monthly salary of $400, paid on the 1st and 15th by Wise or PayPal
Paid time off and paid holidays after 90 days
Bonus for each new clipper you train
Short paid trial period to start

Send:

A short note about yourself and your experience
Your country and time zone

Any pages or accounts you’ve run, if you have them

title: Clipper/Clipping expert wanted

About the role

We're looking for an experienced clipper who turns long-form footage into short-form videos that stop the scroll on YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Instagram Reels. This is a freelance role, paid per video, with a high bar for quality.
We're a digital agency that also builds its own products. In the first phase you'll clip content for those products, working closely with us on hooks, pacing and style. • Up-to-date knowledge of trends, formats and how each platform's algorithm treats content
• Reliability with deadlines and clear communication, since you'll work remotely and largely independently
• Good written English for captions and on-screen text

Nice to have

title: Viral Video Clipper
description:
We’re looking for a high-level short-form video clipper who understands what makes content go viral. 

This is NOT just a video editing position.

What You'll Do
- Create 3–5 short-form videos per day, Monday–Friday
- Find the best clips/moments inside long-form footage
- Restructure dialogue when necessary to create a stronger story
- Identify powerful hooks that stop the scroll
- Make sure every video communicates a FULL, COMPLETE thought
- Understand the client/topic enough to recognize what viewers will actually care about
- Perform basic editing in Adobe Premiere Pro or similar software

Every clip should follow:

HOOK → STORY/CONTEXT → PAYOFF

We do NOT want random clips, unfinished thoughts, or videos that require viewers to watch another video to understand the point.

Compensation
Base compensation is up to $30 per completed video, depending on your skill level and performance.    

But here's where this position gets interesting:

We want to heavily reward editors who consistently find viral content.

If you have a talent for finding clips that generate millions of views, you should make significantly more money.

We want someone who thinks:
“How do I make this video impossible to scroll past?”

—not simply:
“How do I finish my edits for today?”

Requirements
You must:
- Be highly fluent in English
- Understand American conversational English, context, humor, and phrasing
- Understand short-form storytelling and viral content
- Be capable of producing at least 3–5 clips per day
- Have basic professional video-editing skills
- Be dependable and able to hit deadlines consistently

How to Apply

Your finished video must be 59 seconds or less and demonstrate your ability to identify and structure:

Hook → Context → Payoff

We are not looking for crazy effects or fancy editing. We care much more about what you choose to clip and how you structure the content.

title: Fix our AI video clip pipeline: faster, fewer errors
description:
We make short-form product videos with AI. I built an internal app (with Claude Code) that plans videos, generates AI clips through Higgsfield, edits them with ffmpeg, and prepares them for posting. Clip generation was too slow and failed too often, so it is currently switched off.

YOUR JOB: FIX IT. Not a report. Working results.

THE APP
Python (FastAPI), plain JavaScript, Supabase (Postgres and storage), Vercel, and a background worker on a cloud Mac. There is a detailed handoff doc, and I will give you our current numbers on clip speed and failures.

WHAT "DONE" MEANS
- Clip generation is back on and works.
- Clips are generated in parallel, not one at a time.
- Failed clips retry automatically, and we never pay twice for the same clip.
- When something fails, the app shows a clear reason.

title: Build video-clip sourcing, identification and editing platform (Python/Node, Docker)
description:
Overview:
We run a small content team that finds short movie/TV clips on Instagram, locates the scene in our own full-length source files, edits it into a vertical captioned reel, and publishes it. We have a detailed spec in two phases and want a fixed-price quote for EACH phase separately, plus a total.

PHASE 1 — core platform

1. Sourcing
   - Pull Instagram reels from a list of accounts and hashtags on a schedule, using a scraping API (Apify or similar).
   - Store post, metrics and thumbnail; dedupe near-identical videos with perceptual hashing.
   - Daily cost cap on scraping spend.

2. Identification
   - For each reel, identify the film or TV show, and for TV the season and episode.
   - Match the reel's dialogue against subtitle text (OpenSubtitles) to confirm the episode and the moment, with picture matching as fallback.
   - Show title and start–end timestamp on the reel card; "Find it again" and manual override.

3. Auto-edit and render
   - Cut the matched scene from our source file (cloud storage), overlay captions/subtitles, export vertical 9:16 with ffmpeg.
   - Finished videos kept in a library.

4. Review dashboard (web app)
   - Pipeline stages: To review → To record → To caption → Ready to post → Posted, with counts per stage, approve/skip, client filter.
   - Per-operator queues; admin sees everyone.
   - Work log per operator — clock in / clock out and a record of what each person reviewed, recorded, captioned and posted.
   - Activity feed explaining what the system did and why.
   - Pages: Reels, Library, Imports, Clients, Analytics, Operators, Inbox, Settings. Team accounts with roles.

5. Deployment
   - Docker Compose on one dedicated Linux server: Postgres, API, workers, gateway, logging, nightly backups, automated tests.

PHASE 2 — advanced editing and precision

6. Multi-scene editing
   - Build one reel from several scenes across different films or episodes: pick scenes, order them, trim each, auto-join with transitions, captions across the whole cut.

7. Exact-moment identification
   - Frame-accurate start/end timestamp in the source file, not just the approximate scene; confidence score; target zero confidently-wrong results on a labelled test set we provide.

What I’m providing:

The voiceover track (attached, ~50 sec) — the opening of a Blockbuster downfall video
A full line-by-line edit blueprint (attached doc) with the exact VO, the four beats, and notes on cuts, b-roll, graphics, and sound for each moment

What to deliver:

A finished edit of this ~50-second opening, cut to the provided voiceover
Footage/b-roll on every line, the stat graphics (template-based stat cards are fine), sound design, and a color grade
Export-ready: 1080p, 16:9, H.264 MP4

Read the blueprint — but here’s what I’m judging, in order:

The first 10 seconds. The hook is a Blockbuster card dropping in silence — no music, no intro, no logo. If you slap music over it or add an intro, that’s an automatic fail.
Pacing. A visual on every line, cuts riding the voiceover, no dead frames.
The contrast cut from giant Blockbuster to tiny Netflix — does the edit make me feel the size gap?
Sound design — music ducked under the VO, and the scripted silences preserved.
Footage sourcing — licensed and clean, not random low-res clips. (Use licensed/editorial footage or silhouettes — no unlicensed photos of the real founders or execs.)

Why this matters: This 50-second cut tells me almost everything about whether you can handle the full 11–13 min video. If the opening lands, the ongoing role is yours.

title: n8n automation: Google Drive to Claude captions to GoHighLevel Social Planner
description:
Title: n8n automation: Google Drive to Claude captions to GoHighLevel Social Planner

I run a wellness and fitness brand and need an experienced n8n builder to set up one workflow on n8n Cloud. Fixed price preferred. I want to be able to maintain and troubleshoot this myself after it's built, so teaching is a big part of this job.

What the workflow needs to do:

1. Watch several Google Drive folders. Each folder is an "asset bucket" for a type of social media content (for example, dancer foot pain or active adult balance).
2. When a new video or image is added, create a row in a Google Sheet with basic info based on which folder it came from.
3. Send the file name and that bucket's caption instructions to Claude (Anthropic API) to write a social caption and a first comment, then add both to the row. Each bucket will have its own instructions, hook style, and comment keyword.
4. Upload the file to the GoHighLevel media library through the GHL API (using a Private Integration token) and write the GHL media link back into the sheet. Google Drive links do not work for this, so the GHL link is required.
5. The finished sheet needs to match the format of GoHighLevel Social Planner's advanced bulk upload, so I can upload posts in bulk.

I currently have a Google Workspace Studio flow that handles part of step 2. You can replace it if keeping everything in n8n is cleaner.

Build requirements:
- Proven experience with n8n and the GoHighLevel API, especially media uploads
- Experience connecting n8n to the Anthropic (Claude) API
- Build and test on a copy of my sheet before touching the real one
- Clear error notifications sent to me by email or text, written in plain language, saying which step failed and which file it was

Training and handoff (required):
- A live screen share session (about 1 hour) where you teach me how to read n8n's execution log, find which step failed, and fix the common problems
- A written troubleshooting guide covering the most likely breaks, such as an expired Google connection, an expired or changed GHL token, an empty Anthropic API balance, a file that's too large or the wrong format, and a renamed sheet column
- A recorded walkthrough showing how to edit caption instructions and add a new bucket
- 30 days of support after handoff for questions or fixes

To apply, please include:
- Your fixed price and timeline
- A similar automation you've built, especially anything involving GoHighLevel
